sections.heading: Heroku limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Does not outrank Render (7.9) as the cloud-paas award; Eco list price dynos sleep after 30 minutes of inactivity and are personal-only — not always-on production; Basic list price is the always-on floor; No forever-free dyno (hasFreePlan false) because it forces process changes or add-ons around Heroku when infrastructure monitoring is the job.

Pricing interpretation: no free plan confirmed — scope a paid pilot on Eco with exit criteria before annual seats.

Plan trade-off: you gain infrastructure monitoring at the expense of Per-agent vs per-host vs per-seat vs per-GB pricing models — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Eco · infrastructure monitoring | Basic | Standard-1X.

Alternative context: unlike Render, Heroku is preferable when Teams that want Salesforce-backed Cedar dynos with a published Basic list price always-on floor because infrastructure monitoring plus infrastructure monitoring match; prefer Render when Teams that need a forever-free dyno or Hobby-credit evaluation path because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for Heroku
sections.body:
Scenario: recommend Heroku for Teams that want Salesforce-backed Cedar dynos with a published Basic list price always-on floor; do not choose it when Teams that need a forever-free dyno or Hobby-credit evaluation path — the jobs diverge at infrastructure monitoring.

Implementation time: weeks to configure infrastructure monitoring if Github must be green before invites.

Integrations in research: Github.

Decision conclusion: buy Heroku when researched fit (Teams that want Salesforce-backed Cedar dynos with a published Basic list price always-on floor) beats researched limits (Does not outrank Render (7.9) as the cloud-paas award); otherwise keep researching — do not substitute product names into a generic setup essay.
